findings.title: Same-key index builds are no longer single-flighted
findings.body: BuildIndex used to hold cacheMu for the whole build, so a second GetIndex blocked until the finished index was published. The mutex is now taken only around the cache insert. getOrCreateIndex still does check-then-act (GetIndex, and on a miss build) and even has a TODO that same-key builds must not run together. After startup, two Search calls, or a Search and a watch event, for a namespace that was not built during init (count at or below InitMinCount) both see a cache miss and both call BuildIndex. Memory indexes both succeed and the later cache write overwrites the earlier one without closing it, so documents already written to the discarded index disappear from search and the Bleve index is leaked. File indexes both call bleve.New on the same directory; the loser fails with a path-exists error, so the caller gets a search error even if the other build published a usable index. Parallel builds of different keys are fine, but same-key builds need a per-key lock or singleflight held from the existence check through cache publish.

findings.title: Search index misses writes committed during startup indexing
findings.body: init lists every namespace and only afterward calls WatchWriteEvents. That snapshot records the latest resource version and the SQL poller only returns history newer than that snapshot. The RV returned by build is discarded. Any create, update, or delete committed after a namespace was listed and before the watch snapshot, including writes from other HA replicas, is neither in the bulk index nor replayed. The watch starts only after the slowest namespace finishes, so namespaces that finished early have a gap as long as the rest of the index build, which is the long operation this change is about. Search will keep serving missing, stale, or already-deleted objects until that document is written again. Record the RV before listing, or buffer watch events first, and replay history from that RV after the bulk load.

findings.title: Parallel index builders share err and can hide failures
findings.body: Each errgroup worker assigns s.build's result to the outer err variable and then returns err. When WorkerThreads is greater than 1 those goroutines race on that variable. A failed build can return nil if another worker stores nil into err before the return, so group.Wait succeeds and NewResourceServer starts with some namespaces never indexed. A successful worker can also return another worker's error and fail startup. This is a real data race, not just a logic race. totalBatchesIndexed is incremented from the same goroutines with no synchronization, so the trace attribute is racy as well. Use a local error inside the closure and an atomic counter.

findings.title: Search watch loop panics when the event channel closes
findings.body: After indexing, init starts a goroutine that loops on v := <-events and calls handleEvent, using context.Background rather than the server context. The SQL backend poller closes that channel when the backend stops (it selects on backend done and defers close). A receive on a closed channel yields a nil event, and handleEvent immediately reads evt.Type, which panics. An unrecovered goroutine panic crashes the process during graceful shutdown, skipping the rest of cleanup. server.Stop cannot stop the loop because it only cancels s.ctx. The loop must exit when the channel is closed or the context is cancelled, and the watch must be tied to the server lifetime.

findings.title: File-backed indexes cannot be reopened, so restart fails startup
findings.body: When size is above FileThreshold (the zero value is 0, so any positive count takes this branch unless the option is overridden), BuildIndex calls bleve.New on a directory under Root and never bleve.Open. bleve.New fails if that path already exists, and a failed builder returns without closing the index or removing a partial directory. Init now runs inside NewResourceServer and any error aborts construction, so a restart after a successful file index, or a retry after a build that left the directory behind, cannot start the storage server. The comment that was removed even said the last RV should be checked so an unchanged index can be skipped. Open an existing index when the directory is present, and delete or uniquely name the directory if a build fails, or every file-backed namespace wedges process startup.

findings.title: Init failure in the constructor leaks the backend and watchers
findings.body: NewResourceServer calls Init and, on error, logs and returns nil without calling cancel or Stop. lifecycle.Init may already have opened the database. If search.init succeeded and initWatcher then failed, search.init has already started a WatchWriteEvents poller and an event goroutine on context.Background. The caller never receives the server, so it cannot Stop those resources, and the connection pool and pollers live until the process exits. On the error path, stop the lifecycle/backend and cancel the server context, while still returning the original init error.

findings.title: Startup index build cannot be cancelled or given a deadline
findings.body: The context now used for the full index build is created from context.Background inside NewResourceServer, which does not accept a caller context. The only cancel is Stop, and Stop cannot run until NewResourceServer returns, which is blocked on GetResourceStats and every ListIterator in the index build. A stuck database call therefore hangs process startup with no deadline, and a shutdown signal cannot abort the build. The old request context cancelled too early; this replacement needs a long but bounded startup context that process shutdown can cancel.

findings.title: TotalDocs ranges the index cache without holding cacheMu
findings.body: TotalDocs iterates b.cache with no RLock, while BuildIndex writes that map under cacheMu. Narrowing the lock means builds now publish into the map concurrently, during startup and for later cold namespaces. In Go, a concurrent map read and write is a fatal runtime error, not a missed update. init also calls TotalDocs immediately after starting the watch goroutine that can BuildIndex on a cache miss, and TotalDocs is part of the SearchBackend interface so any other caller can hit the same crash. Hold cacheMu.RLock for the whole iteration.

findings.title: Storage-server integration test is skipped on Postgres
findings.body: TestIntegrationWillRunInstrumentationServerWhenTargetHasNoHttpServer is the integration coverage for the storage-server target, and this PR makes that target initialize unified storage and build the search index during construction. The change skips the test whenever GRAFANA_TEST_DB is postgres, with a TODO that it fails in Drone but works locally. Postgres is a primary deployment database, so CI no longer runs storage-server startup there, and a startup regression from eager init will not be caught. Fix the Postgres failure instead of skipping it.
